summary: Modern databases have evolved far beyond simple data storage, now embedding sophisticated AI and ML capabilities directly into the data platform to eliminate the need to move data to external systems. From native LLM integrations and vector search to in-database model training and inference, these platforms allow developers and data scientists to run AI workloads where the data already lives. This convergence of databases and AI dramatically reduces latency, simplifies architecture, and lowers the barrier to building intelligent applications.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.description: Snowflake Cortex AI provides a suite of fully managed ML and LLM functions directly within Snowflake SQL. It includes COMPLETE() for LLM text generation, SENTIMENT() and SUMMARIZE() for NLP tasks, CLASSIFY_TEXT() for zero-shot classification, and Cortex Search for hybrid vector + keyword search. Cortex Analyst enables natural language querying of structured data. Models from Mistral, Meta Llama, Reka, and others are available without any infrastructure management. Fine-tuning is supported via Cortex Fine-tuning, and ML functions like FORECAST() and ANOMALY_DETECTION() handle time-series use cases natively.
databases.llm_integration: Native support for Mistral Large/7B, Meta Llama 3.1/3.3 (8B, 70B, 405B), Reka Flash, Snowflake Arctic, and others via Cortex LLM functions. Models are called directly in SQL using functions like SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.COMPLETE(). Cortex Search provides hybrid retrieval combining dense vector and BM25 keyword search for RAG pipelines.
databases.pricing_notes: Priced in Snowflake credits. LLM functions are billed per token processed (e.g., Llama 3.1 8B costs ~0.0000225 credits per token). Cortex Search is billed for documents indexed and queries served. ML functions like FORECAST() are billed per compute credit. Costs vary significantly by model size and region. Free tier available for trial accounts.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.description: BigQuery ML allows users to create, train, and run ML models directly using standard SQL syntax, supporting logistic regression, k-means clustering, matrix factorization, boosted trees (XGBoost), deep neural networks (DNNs/AutoML), and time-series ARIMA+ forecasting. Through native Vertex AI integration, BigQuery can call hosted Gemini models for text generation, embeddings, and multimodal tasks via ML.GENERATE_TEXT() and ML.EMBED_TEXT(). Vector search is supported via the VECTOR_SEARCH() function and native vector indexes on BigQuery tables, enabling scalable approximate nearest-neighbor search for RAG architectures.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Google Vertex AI and Gemini models (Gemini 1.5 Flash, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Gemini 2.0). Remote models are registered as BigQuery ML models via CREATE MODEL with REMOTE_WITH_CONNECTION. ML.GENERATE_TEXT() enables text generation and ML.EMBED_TEXT() produces vector embeddings in SQL. Supports PaLM 2 legacy models and open models hosted on Vertex AI Model Garden including Llama and Mistral variants.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML model training is free for linear/logistic regression; AutoML and DNN training incur Vertex AI training costs. Inference via GENERATE_TEXT() is billed at Vertex AI pricing per 1K characters or tokens depending on model (e.g., Gemini 1.5 Flash is ~$0.075/1M input tokens). Vector index creation and VECTOR_SEARCH queries are billed as standard BigQuery compute (on-demand: $6.25/TB scanned or flat-rate slots). BigQuery ML predictions are billed per query.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.description: pgvector is an open-source PostgreSQL extension that adds a native vector data type and enables exact and approximate nearest-neighbor search using IVFFLAT and HNSW indexing algorithms, making PostgreSQL a capable vector database for semantic search and RAG applications. pgai (developed by Timescale) extends this by enabling direct calls to external LLM APIs (OpenAI, Ollama, Cohere, Anthropic) from within SQL functions, allowing embedding generation, text completion, and model inference without leaving the database. Together they allow developers to store embeddings alongside relational data and query them with standard SQL joins and filters.
databases.llm_integration: pgai provides SQL wrapper functions to call OpenAI (text-embedding-3-small, GPT-4o), Ollama (local models), Anthropic Claude, Cohere, and others directly from PostgreSQL functions. For example, ai.openai_embed() generates embeddings inline during INSERT or SELECT. Vectorizer (part of pgai) automates embedding creation and synchronization for table columns. No native LLM hosting — it proxies to external APIs using stored API keys in database secrets.
databases.pricing_notes: Both pgvector and pgai are open-source (PostgreSQL License and Apache 2.0 respectively) and free to install on any self-hosted PostgreSQL instance. When using managed services like Timescale Cloud, Supabase, or AWS RDS/Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector, you pay standard compute/storage fees for the database instance. LLM API calls made through pgai are billed directly by the respective provider (e.g., OpenAI API pricing). No additional licensing fees for the extensions themselves.

databases.name: Amazon (Aurora ML + Redshift ML)
databases.ai_feature: Aurora ML + Redshift ML + Amazon Bedrock Integration
databases.description: Aurora ML enables Amazon Aurora (MySQL and PostgreSQL-compatible) to invoke ML models hosted on Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Comprehend directly via SQL functions, allowing sentiment analysis, fraud detection, and custom inference without ETL. Redshift ML allows Amazon Redshift users to create, train, and deploy ML models using SQL with CREATE MODEL syntax, automatically leveraging SageMaker Autopilot under the hood. Both services also integrate with Amazon Bedrock for generative AI capabilities including text generation, summarization, and embedding generation from foundation models, and pgvector support is available on Aurora PostgreSQL for vector workloads.
databases.llm_integration: Amazon Bedrock integration allows Aurora and Redshift to call foundation models including Amazon Titan (text and embeddings), Anthropic Claude 2/3, Meta Llama 3, Mistral, Cohere Command, and AI21 Jurassic via SQL. Aurora PostgreSQL supports pgvector extension for vector storage and similarity search. Redshift supports vector data types and cosine/L2 similarity functions. SageMaker-hosted custom models can be invoked from both Aurora and Redshift via IAM-authorized endpoints.
databases.pricing_notes: Aurora ML incurs charges for SageMaker inference endpoint usage (per hour per instance) plus standard Aurora compute/storage costs. Redshift ML charges for SageMaker Autopilot training jobs (per training hour) plus Redshift compute costs; predictions themselves are free after model deployment if using built-in prediction function. Bedrock API calls are billed per token/character by model (e.g., Claude 3 Sonnet ~$3/1M input tokens). pgvector on Aurora PostgreSQL has no additional cost beyond instance pricing. Free tier available for new AWS accounts on eligible services.

databases.name: Databricks (MLflow + DBRX)
databases.ai_feature: Databricks AI — MLflow, DBRX, Mosaic AI, Unity Catalog AI
databases.description: Databricks offers one of the most comprehensive in-platform AI ecosystems. MLflow (open-source, created by Databricks) provides end-to-end ML lifecycle management including experiment tracking, model registry, and serving. Mosaic AI (formerly Databricks ML) includes AutoML for automated model building, Feature Store for feature management, Model Serving for low-latency inference endpoints, and AI Playground for LLM experimentation. DBRX is Databricks' own open-source mixture-of-experts LLM optimized for enterprise use. Vector Search is a native managed vector database built into Unity Catalog. Databricks also supports fine-tuning, RAG pipeline construction, and agent frameworks via LangChain and LlamaIndex integrations.
databases.llm_integration: Databricks Model Serving hosts DBRX, Meta Llama 3 (8B, 70B), Mistral, MPT, and other open models as pay-per-token APIs. External model integrations support OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, and Amazon Bedrock through the AI Gateway (MLflow Gateway). Databricks Vector Search integrates with embedding models to auto-sync Delta Lake tables into searchable vector indexes. Foundation Model APIs provide standardized OpenAI-compatible endpoints. LangChain and LlamaIndex have native Databricks integrations for building RAG and agent workflows.
databases.pricing_notes: MLflow is fully open-source and free. Managed MLflow on Databricks is included with the platform at no extra charge. Foundation Model API (DBRX, Llama) is billed per token (e.g., DBRX Instruct ~$0.75/1M input tokens, $2.25/1M output tokens). Vector Search is billed by DBUs (Databricks Units) per hour for the index pipeline plus storage. Model Serving endpoints are billed per DBU-hour of compute. Databricks uses a subscription model with DBU pricing that varies by cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP) and tier (Standard, Premium, Enterprise). Free trial available.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search + AI Integrations
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search enables storing vector embeddings as fields within MongoDB documents alongside their source data and metadata, then performing approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) search using HNSW indexing at scale. This makes it straightforward to build semantic search and RAG applications without a separate vector database. Queries use the $vectorSearch aggregation stage, allowing vector search to be combined with Atlas full-text search ($search), geospatial filters, and standard MongoDB query operators in a single pipeline. Atlas also integrates with major LLM frameworks and offers Atlas Stream Processing and Data API for real-time AI application backends.
databases.llm_integration: MongoDB Atlas does not host LLMs natively but provides first-class integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack, Spring AI, and Semantic Kernel, positioning Atlas as the vector store layer in RAG architectures. Native connectors exist for OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Cohere, Hugging Face, Google Vertex AI, and Amazon Bedrock for embedding generation workflows. The Atlas Data API and MongoDB Drivers allow any LLM application to read/write embeddings programmatically. Atlas Charts and no-code AI application templates are available for rapid prototyping.
databases.pricing_notes: Vector Search indexing is available on M10+ dedicated clusters (starting ~$0.08/hour for M10 on AWS). Free shared tier (M0) does not support Vector Search indexes. Pricing is based on the underlying Atlas cluster tier (compute + storage) with no separate per-query charge for vector search operations — queries consume normal cluster resources. Data transfer and backup costs apply per standard Atlas pricing. Serverless instances have limited Vector Search support. Enterprise agreements available for large deployments. Free $200 credit available for new Atlas accounts.
